title: Praeceptum Quando Iussi Sunt Omnes Episcopi Cellulanos Habere
author: Ennodius
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0114a.stoa014.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's CSEL.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: certe uel si mens sit recti conscia, uindicta dignus est qui alii existit causa periculi: dum enim suspicionibus patefacit accessum, fit fraterni origo discriminis, et qui peccandi fomenta tribuit ipse iugulum morti inpingit, ut ait diuinus et beatus praeco: noli detrahere, ne eradiceris, confessor Ambrosius: multi non dederunt errori locum, et dederunt suspicioni. suspicio ista est interitus suspicantis atque eam non caret peccato qui dederit. unde mansuro cum dei et redemptoris nostri ordinatione constituto sancimus, apostolicae sedis beati Petri uel praesulis eius papae auctoritate subnixi, quae, uitia desiderat radicitus amputari, ut nullus religiosorum de memoratis ordinibus aliter quam, praefati sumus audeat conuersari, uel quicumque praesumpserint cum amissione pudoris honorum damna sustineant.
passages.english: Certainly, even if the mind is conscious of what is right, he deserves punishment who becomes for another the cause of danger: for while he opens the way to suspicions, he becomes the origin of a brother's peril, and he who supplies the kindling for sin himself thrusts his throat toward death, as the divine and blessed herald says: "Do not slander, lest you be uprooted"; [and] the confessor Ambrose: "Many have given no room to error, and yet have given [it] to suspicion. That suspicion is the ruin of the one who suspects, and he who has given [occasion for] it is not free of sin." Therefore by an enactment that is to endure, with the ordinance of God and our Redeemer, we decree, supported by the authority of the apostolic see of blessed Peter and of its prelate the pope, which desires vices to be cut off at the root, that none of the religious of the aforementioned orders should dare to live otherwise than we have stated above, or [that] whoever presume [to do so] should suffer the loss of their honours together with the loss of their good name.
passages.notes: "atque eam non caret peccato qui dederit": the text seems faulty; translated as if "et eam qui dederit non caret peccato". "quae, uitia" and "quam, praefati sumus" have misplaced commas, apparently for "quae uitia" and "quam praefati sumus"; translated accordingly. The "divine and blessed herald" is not named; the quotation resembles Proverbs (cf. 24:21–22 / 2:22 in Latin versions) but is unidentified here. "pudoris" rendered "good name" (sense of shame/honour).
